Alex, thanks for the details — helpful. Looping in Marissa (CS) and Karthik (solutions) for the rollout specifics and cost ops. Quick answers up front and a short ask list so we can give a concrete proposal: 

Prelim answers:
- Yes, Dedicated supports a transient burst pool (reserved but idle-able GPUs that can be added to your pool for short windows).
- Autoscale speed depends on instance type and provisioning mode; typical cold add for GPU nodes: ~3–8 mins for node provision + model coldstart. With pre-warmed images and cached KV we can get effective capacity in ~2–4 mins for common sequences.
- To avoid cold-start tail latency we recommend a small pre-warm runway (scheduled or event-triggered) and prefix KV caching for expected prompt sets.
- SLA exception for short overage is doable as a contractual add-on; we can draft a temporary burst allowance tied to the launch window.

Proposed preliminary sizing (very rough):
- Baseline reserved: 40 A100-equivalent GPUs (handles steady 40% load comfortably with 25% headroom).
- Transient burst pool: 20 additional A100-equivalent GPUs available for automated attach/detach (up to 60 GPUs total).
- Autoscale policy: step + predictive headroom: up to 10 GPUs/minute, scale step 4 GPUs, cooldown 300s. Burst duration cap: default 48 hrs unless extended by agreement.

Ask list for accuracy:
1) Can you share a 1-week minute-level traffic sample (or an hour-by-hour ramp) — rough CSV is fine.
2) Which exact model variant (name/size/quantization) will you run in production?
3) Any data locality / private VPC constraints?

I attached a sample CSV template and a quick capacity diagram (capacity_architecture_v1.png). We can convert this into a formal AMP (Mutual Action Plan) after you confirm traffic and model.

— Vivek

Quick internal notes on customer guarantees and risk mitigation before we send the formal quote. Quoting Vivek below.

- SLA / SLO: For a launch like this we should propose a temporary SLA extension that explicitly covers burst attachment latency and max transient queues. Procurement will want a guaranteed response (e.g., <200ms median token latency at peak, allowances for up to 5% p99 degradation during attach windows).
- Canary + Rollout: We'll recommend a phased canary during the ramp: 10% of traffic to the new Dedicated group for the first 2 hours, then 50%, then full. This reduces single-point failure risk for the launch.
- Fallback policy: Auto-fallback to hosted Redwood models in other regions if we can't attach burst capacity fast enough. Need legal signoff on data plane boundary for that path.

Karthik, can you confirm the autoscale knobs and minimum pre-warm runway we should document for engineering handoff? Also include estimated cost delta for a 48-hr 20-GPU burst vs. reserved capacity.

-Marissa

Marissa / team — technical details to include in the proposal and the config we recommend for the Dedicated fleet: 

Autoscale & burst config (recommendation):
- Metrics: request_concurrency (per-model) + queue_depth + 1-min token throughput. Use a composite signal where concurrency AND queue depth must exceed thresholds to trigger burst attachment (reduces noisy scaling).
- Scale step: 4 GPUs. Max attach rate: 10 GPUs/min (backed by infra tests).
- Cooldown: 300s (5m) between scale actions to avoid oscillation.
- Pre-warm: scheduled pre-warm window 30–60 minutes before expected ramp (can be event-triggered via webhook), start with 8 GPUs pre-warmed (hot-image + cached KV).
- Burst pool policy: auto-attach up to 20 GPUs, with an admin override to extend to 40 for emergency (manual approval). Burst duration: default 48 hrs, with billing pro-rated to minute.
- Fallback: if attach latency > 8 mins, redirect new requests to cross-region hosted endpoints with a token-sanitization proxy (legal to confirm).

Operational notes:
- Monitoring: expose per-route token-per-second and per-gpu-util metrics; set automated alerts at 70/85/95%.
- Cost controls: soft cap on burst spend, hard cap requiring manual owner approval.
- Testing: run an infra load test simulating 6x ramp; results show attach median 3m50s on our pre-warm friendly images.

I'll draft the autoscale JSON snippet we use for Dedicated policy and attach it to the AMP.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
